politician.name: Mike Minogue
politician.bio: Mike Minogue is a businessman and U.S. Army veteran who served in Operation Desert Storm and later led the Danvers-based medical device company Abiomed as president and CEO from 2004 until its acquisition by Johnson & Johnson in 2022. A first-time candidate, he entered the 2026 race for governor in October 2025 and won the Republican nomination over Brian Shortsleeve in the September 2026 primary. He is challenging incumbent Democratic Gov. Maura Healey in the Nov. 3, 2026 general election.

summary:
Minogue and Gov. Maura Healey met Oct. 15 for their second and final debate, clashing over the cost of living, energy, housing, immigration and government accountability [1][2]. Minogue called for cutting the gas tax and utility fees, blamed Healey for blocking natural gas pipelines as attorney general, and pressed her over a fired aide facing drug and fraud charges [2][3]. PolitiFact found his pipeline and electricity-cost claims accurate but said his attacks over the aide and his use of a Healey quote needed context [3]. On abortion, Minogue said he would follow the law regardless of his personal beliefs, while Healey said he does not trust women, a charge he called a cheap shot [1].

On Oct. 18, running mate Shawn Oliver suspended his lieutenant governor campaign after being charged with OUI after a crash in New Bedford; he pleaded not guilty, after Minogue publicly urged him to step aside and said he would seek Oliver's resignation if both won [4]. Oliver's name remains on the ballot, and Republicans quoted by the Globe were split between calling the episode an unforced error and predicting little effect on the governor's race [4]. Minogue later said Oliver would not serve as his lieutenant governor and urged voters not to cross Oliver's name off their ballots, warning it could invalidate their vote [7][8].

A UMass Amherst/WCVB poll taken Oct. 5-12 showed Healey leading Minogue 57% to 32% [5], and a Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll released Oct. 20 put her lead at 23 points, with 21% of likely voters saying they had not heard of him [8]. After casting his early ballot in Hamilton on Oct. 22, Minogue dismissed the public polls and cited internal campaign polling he said showed a single-digit race, which his campaign did not immediately provide [8]. He spent a record $6.1 million for a gubernatorial candidate in a single month (September), and Healey's campaign criticized his donations to a committee that backed President Trump [8]. A pro-Minogue super PAC also began targeting independent candidate Andrea James with ads and mailers; its chairman called it a matter of principle, while one political scientist said it appeared aimed at drawing votes away from Healey [6].

In a live Boston 25 News interview, Minogue called for eliminating the state's 24-cent gas tax, said he would never raise taxes, and pledged to forgo a governor's salary and have an outside firm audit every state agency [7]. He listed disagreements with Trump on tariffs, rhetoric, the trade dispute with Canada and NIH cuts, and said immigration enforcement should be coordinated with local officials and prioritize violent criminals and drug dealers [2][7].

citations.title: Healey, Minogue clash over costs, housing and energy in final Massachusetts gubernatorial debate

citations.title: Fact-checking Healey, Minogue in final MA governor debate
citations.snippet: Fact-checks the final debate, finding Minogue's claims on Healey's past pipeline opposition and the state's high electricity costs accurate, while saying his claims about a fired aide and a clipped Healey quote needed context.

citations.title: Shawn Oliver suspends lieutenant governor campaign after OUI charge
